Design concept:

"The Sims neighborhood where every house is a Doom level" — top-down neighborhood overworld (Sims-like, isometric-ish 3D) with houses on plots. Walk your Sim around the neighborhood. Enter a house → it becomes a first-person Doom-style level with corridor/rooms, demons, shotgun, health, armor, keys, doors, exit.

This is ambitious but doable. Scope:

1. Neighborhood view: 3D low-poly suburban neighborhood with road, sidewalk, lots, houses, trees, street lamps, mailbox, sky, clouds. A controllable Sim character in third person (WASD / touch joystick). Camera follows. Hovering house shows "ENTER: Doom". Approach door and press E to load that house's Doom level.

2. Doom level mode: first-person raycast? Use 3D geometry with first-person controls, enemies (billboard sprite demons drawn via canvas textures? or low-poly geometry). Shooting with hitscan, muzzle flash, weapon sprite drawn as DOM/canvas overlay with procedural pixel-art shotgun. HUD with health, armor, ammo, keys, face portrait. Doors that open, keys, enemies that chase, pickups, exit portal.

3. Persistence: each house cleared status saved in localStorage, neighborhood shows "CLEARED" signs / lights. Stats: kills, secrets.

4. Multiple houses with distinct level themes (e.g., "The Brady Bunker", "Grandma's Hellmouth", "The Split-Level of Sin", "Cul-de-Sac of Carnage"). Each generates a different level layout via seeded procedural generation + handcrafted-ish rooms.

5. Mobile: touch joystick + fire button; responsive HUD; safe areas.

6. Audio: WebAudio procedural — shotgun blast, demon growl, pickup chime, ambient drone. Mute toggle.

7. Polish: title screen with neighborhood name "WHISPERING PINES ESTATES", loading, pause menu, pointer lock, minimap in Doom mode, objective text, level intro card, damage flash, kill counter, exit.

Technical approach: Three.js ES module bundled via vite? If using plain static, can download three.module.js into vendor. Let's do static with importmap. Simpler start (no npm install issues), and default-start supports 'html'. But three's module file ~1.2MB, fine.

Neighborhood also could be procedurally modeled geometry: houses with gabled roofs, windows emissive, hedges, fences, driveways, pool, cul-de-sac loop.

Camera: third-person, near top-down (Sims style) with orbit control? Sims 3 style: angled isometric-ish; player character. I'll do a follow camera with mouse-drag rotate and zoom. Player movement WASD relative to camera.

Entering house: fade to black, switch scene to level. Level built on a grid with walls extruded (Doom-like blocky). Use textured materials procedurally generated (hell walls, tech panels, doors). Add ceiling/floor. Enemy AI: move toward player on grid with simple collision, attack when close, ranged projectiles maybe. Hitscan weapons.

Implement collision: AABB circle vs wall grid. Level grid e.g. 40x40 cells of 2.5 units. Walls from grid. Door cells with open animation. Keys as colored keycards. Exit switch.

Enemies: imps (ranged fireball), zombies (hitscan slower), pinky demons (fast melee). Spawn positions from level gen. Health, hit flash, death animation (sprite squish + fade), drop.

Objective per house: kill all demons, find key, reach exit portal. Or simpler: kill the "house boss" and exit. Let's do: collect the house key from key room, open exit door, step into exit → level complete, "Property Cleared" and back to neighborhood. Kills optional for rating.

Reward: after clearing, house gets sold sign / lights turn on / lawn flamingo? Fun: each cleared house emits smoke-free and lawn gets "SOLD" sign; neighborhood "curse meter" decreases. Let me design the game thoroughly, then write code.

## Core concept

Title: "WHISPERING PINES: Open House of the Damned" or "CUL-DE-SAC OF THE DAMNED". Neighborhood named "Whispering Pines Estates". Each house is a Doom level. Player is a real-estate agent? Sims-style. Story: You're a prospective homebuyer / "HOA Enforcer". Every house has a portal to hell in the basement.

Overworld: third-person Sim with plumbob (green diamond) above head — very Sims. Neighborhood with cul-de-sac, 4-5 houses, street, sidewalks, trees, parked car, lamp posts, community mailbox. Daytime golden sky. Each house has a floating icon showing skull count / status.

Interaction: walk to front door, prompt "[E] Enter — 4BR / 2BA / 1 HELLMOUTH". Click house to walk to it? For accessibility, "Enter" when near. Add "Fast travel" list from a neighborhood map (M) maybe. Mobile: tap door / a big "ENTER" button when near.

Doom level generation:
- Grid maze representing house floorplan in "hell mode": 1 cell = 3 units, wall height 3.2. Layout generated from a seeded recursive-division / rooms + corridors within, with distinct room naming? It's a house in hell: foyer, living room, kitchen, hallway, basement stairs. We can theme rooms and add furniture-esque hell props (tables, barrels, pillars, blood pools, chains, pentagram).
- Use grid-based walls with procedurally textured materials: wallpaper patterns, wood, hellstone, flesh. Different palette per house.
- Doors: normal door cells that open when player approaches (animated slide up? rotate). Locked exit door needs key.
- Key item placed in a far room; exit portal in another. Enemies cover.

Rendering: three.js WebGLRenderer. Fog for atmosphere. Point lights limited (performance). Use emissive materials + ambient + hemi + a flashlight-ish spotlight on camera? Doom has no flashlight typically but we can use a subtle headlamp. Add fog dark red. Flickering light pools.

Enemy sprites: generate pixel-art textures via canvas draw: imp (brown demon with horns), zombie (greenish soldier), pinky (pink beast), maybe "Realtor" ghost. Each has 2-3 frames? Simple bobbing sprite with hit flash and death scaling. Use sprites and raycast hit detection based on screen center or distance-based aim? For FPS feel, do raycast against enemy bounding spheres along camera forward. Sprite hit zones: use sphere radius. Fine.

Weapon: rendered as a 2D overlay in a separate canvas? Simplest: a 3D low-poly shotgun attached to camera with bob and muzzle flash light + shell HUD. Pixel-art weapon drawn on 2D canvas overlay is very Doom. I'll draw procedural pixel-art shotgun on canvas each frame with recoil offset. But scaling at various resolutions. Use DOM image via offscreen canvas with CSS pixelated, redrawn per frame? Better: use a single canvas overlay sized to weapon region and draw. Or draw the gun in a full-screen 2D canvas (HUD canvas) that also draws crosshair and muzzle flash. That's straightforward and performant. HUD DOM for stats.

Music/audio: WebAudio synth ambient + shotgun noise + enemy growls + pickups + door + hurt. Implement compact synth.

Neighborhood movement: third-person character built from primitives (capsule body, head, arms, legs) with walk animation. Plumbob rotates above. Camera at offset behind/above, orbit with mouse drag or Q/E? Use mouse drag to rotate, wheel zoom. WASD relative to camera yaw. On mobile, left joystick moves; drag right area rotates camera.

Doom controls: pointer lock on click; WASD + mouse look; Shift sprint; click fire; 1/2 weapon; E interact/open; Esc pause. Mobile: left joystick move, right area look (touch drag), fire button, use button.

HUD:
- Neighborhood: top-left "WHISPERING PINES ESTATES", curse meter / houses cleared 0/4, a "Neighborhood Map (M)" toggle. Bottom-center interaction prompt. Compass? Coins?
- Doom: bottom bar classic Doom status: AMMO, HEALTH, ARMOR, face, KILLS, and objective top-left; keys icons; minimap top-right (canvas 2D fog-of-war maybe). Message log center-top ("Picked up a shotgun!", "You need the red keycard"). Hit markers/damage vignette.

}

generate() {

    const canH = node.h >= minLeaf*2;
    const canW = node.w >= minLeaf*2;
    if (depth<=0 || (!canH&&!canW)) { leaves.push(node); return; }
    let horiz;

    if (horiz) {

      split({x:node.x,z:node.z,w:node.w,h:cut}, depth-1);
      split({x:node.x,z:node.z+cut,w:node.w,h:node.h-cut}, depth-1);

  };

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D browser game from an empty scaffold matching the prompt: "3D The Sims neighborhood where every house is a Doom level."

## Requirements
- Build now; do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly at the end.
- Must be complete/playable, not a prototype.
- Earlier project conventions included: support desktop and mobile/touch, keep controls within safe areas, use Three.js-style 3D, and verify with browser screenshots that show real geometry.

## Decisions
- Built a static `index.html` + ES modules game using local `vendor/three.module.js` (three r160), served by `default-start.mjs`.
- Concept: "Whispering Pines Estates" cul-de-sac with 5 houses; 4 are haunted Doom levels, the 5th "Model Home" unlocks after clearing 4.
- Neighborhood is third-person Sims-style with plumbob, realtor NPC, map, compass, house markers, save progression.
- Houses become first-person Doom levels via BSP-generated floor plans, doors, props, enemies (zombie/imp/pinky/boss), sigil key, exit portal, minimap, Doom HUD, pixel weapon overlay.
- All art/audio is procedural (canvas textures + WebAudio); no external assets.
- Progress/cleared houses/mute/stats stored in `localStorage` key `whispering-pines-save-v1`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created `index.html`, `style.css`, `vendor/three.module.js`.
- Created `src/textures.js`, `src/audio.js`, `src/world.js`, `src/dungeon.js`, `src/level.js`, `src/game.js`.
- Title screen renders correctly; neighborhood scene renders with houses, NPC, HUD, dialogue, map button, compass.
- Page loads with no reported page errors during title/neighborhood capture.
- Screenshots captured at `screenshots/title/final-desktop.png` and `screenshots/neighborhood/final-desktop.png`.
- Fixed initial runtime bug: moved `placeTorches()` out of `generate()` into `build()` (it used `this.group` before creation).
- Reduced corridors from 2-wide to 1-wide.
- Added pause button (`#pause-btn`) to level HUD with click handler.

### Active
- About to run a custom Playwright level test to verify entering a house, level rendering, movement, and firing.
- Test script created at `/tmp/opencode/test-level.mjs` but not yet executed.

### Blocked
- `playwright-cli` fails because it expects Chromium build `chromium-1243`, but installed build is `chromium-1248`; use the runtime Playwright + `capture.sh` / custom scripts with `config.browser.launchOptions` instead.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D browser game from the empty scaffold matching: "3D The Sims neighborhood where every house is a Doom level."

## Requirements
- Build now; do not ask clarifying questions. Make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly at the end.
- Must be complete/playable, not a prototype.
- Support desktop and mobile/touch; keep controls within safe areas.
- Use Three.js-style 3D and verify with browser screenshots showing real geometry.

## Decisions
- Static `index.html` + ES modules game using local `vendor/three.module.js` (three r160), served by `default-start.mjs`.
- Concept: "Whispering Pines Estates" cul-de-sac with 5 houses; 4 haunted Doom levels, then the 5th "Model Home" unlocks.
- Neighborhood is third-person Sims-style with plumbob, realtor NPC, map, compass, house markers, save progression.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

# Whispering Pines — Every House Is a Doom Level

A complete, playable 3D browser game. Explore a quiet suburban cul-de-sac in third person, then step inside any open house and it becomes a first-person Doom-style level: BSP floor plans, closing doors, sigil keys, demons, a shotgun, a minimap, and an exit portal.

The neighborhood is built with **Three.js** (vendored locally). Every texture, sprite, portrait, and sound is generated at runtime with canvas and WebAudio — there are no external art or audio files.

## Play

Serve the repo root with any static file server and open it in a browser:

```bash
python3 -m http.server 3002
# open http://localhost:3002
```

The provided `start.sh` uses the OMGithub runtime's `default-start.mjs` if you are running inside that environment.

### Desktop

| Input | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `WASD` / arrows | Move |
| Mouse drag (neighborhood) | Orbit camera |
| Mouse (level, pointer lock) | Look |
| Left click | Fire |
| `E` | Interact / advance dialogue |
| `M` | Neighborhood map |
| `1` `2` `3` | Shotgun / pistol / chaingun |
| `Q` | Cycle weapon |
| `Shift` | Sprint |
| `Esc` | Pause / release mouse |
| Wheel (neighborhood) | Zoom camera |

### Mobile / touch

- **Left side drag**: virtual joystick.
- **Right side drag**: look around.
- **FIRE**: fire the current weapon (hold for automatic weapons).
- **USE**: interact, read the objective, or use the portal.
- **SWAP**: cycle weapons.
- **MAP** (neighborhood): open the association directory.
- **ENTER …**: contextual button when standing at a house or NPC.

The layout respects `env(safe-area-inset-*)`, keeps the joystick and action buttons clear of the Doom HUD, and uses touch-native pointer events.

## The neighborhood

Whispering Pines Estates has five properties around a cul-de-sac:

1. **The Split-Level of Sin** — 12 Cursed Court
2. **The Brady Bunker** — 8 Pentagram Place
3. **Casa de Carnage** — 13 Bloodstone Bend
4. **The Open Concept** — 6 Abyss Avenue
5. **The Model Home** — 1 Whispering Pines Way (locked until the other four are cleared)

Each house has a generated layout, a different color/theme, and a rising demon count. The Model Home is the boss level; clearing it triggers the ending and free-roam neighborhood.

## Features

- Third-person Sims-style neighborhood with a plumbob, realtor NPC, house markers, compass, minimap-style directory, and a cursed HOA.
- Five playable first-person houses, each generated from a BSP floor plan with corridors, rooms, doors, torches, hanging lamps, props, and collision.
- Three weapons: shotgun, pistol, and chaingun, with ammo, cooldowns, spread, muzzle flash, recoil, screen shake, and a pixel-art weapon overlay.
- Four enemy archetypes: zombies, imps, pinkies, and the HOA President boss, with projectile attacks, damage, death animations, and sound.
- Sigil key → sealed portal → results → return to neighborhood loop.
- Doom HUD (health, armor, ammo, kills, key), procedural face portrait, hit markers, damage flash, minimap, pause menu, death/retry/flee flow.
- Persistent progression in `localStorage` under `whispering-pines-save-v1`: cleared houses, best times, total kills/time, mute state.
- Responsive title, intro, map, pause, results, death, and ending screens.
- Zero external runtime dependencies beyond the vendored Three.js module.

## Project layout

```
index.html            markup, HUDs, overlays, import map, favicon
style.css             full responsive visual design + touch controls
src/game.js           state machine, input, cameras, HUD, screens, fx, weapon drawing
src/world.js          neighborhood, houses, signs, NPC, colliders, markers
src/dungeon.js        BSP level generation, props, torches, items, enemies, exit
src/level.js          first-person movement, combat, enemy AI, doors, portal, minimap
src/textures.js       procedural canvas textures, signs, sprites, portraits
src/audio.js          procedural WebAudio music, ambience, and sound effects
vendor/three.module.js Three.js r160
```

## Notes and assumptions

- The brief was intentionally open, so the game assumes a single-player, offline, desktop-or-mobile experience with no backend.
- "3D The Sims neighborhood" is interpreted as a third-person explorable cul-de-sac with a realtor NPC and lot markers; "every house is a Doom level" is interpreted literally once you enter.
- Progression is local-only. Clearing houses unlocks the Model Home; no account or network is required.
- The game targets modern evergreen browsers with ES modules, WebGL, and WebAudio. A mouse/keyboard is recommended on desktop; touch controls are enabled automatically for coarse pointers and narrow viewports.
- Audio is unlocked on the first user gesture, as required by browser autoplay policies.
- Deterministic BSP generation uses the house id to seed layouts, so a given property is consistent between visits.
- All art and audio are procedural. Three.js is vendored for offline use.

## Credits

- Three.js r160 (MIT) — `vendor/three.module.js`.
- Everything else — procedural canvas art, WebAudio synthesis, level generation, and game code — was built for this project.

The browser has only one page. Software rendering. It's a one-off. But could real users experience delayed level entry? Probably not; the browser maybe throttled due to low fps. The wait was 10s, then results click hidden? The script error occurred after all? It says results click not visible maybe from another state after loop; but CLEARED includes all 4, so it got through. The error at line 36 might be from the final concept results click? But CLEARED printed after loops, so no. The error stack maybe from the last click because results overlay hidden after click but then `.click` retry? Wait it printed all logs and CLEARED then errors? The tail shows error only. Probably after clicking #results-btn the click action occurred but then the transition hid results, and Playwright considered it not stable? Weird. Not product.

The 10s bunker entry might be because the fade setTimeout gets severely delayed under CPU software rendering when multiple scenes? Or because `buildLevel` for bunker is slow (BSP + textures) and the page is frozen for ~10s. Yes: buildLevel constructs a dungeon and lots of meshes synchronously, about 1-2s on GPU? On software CPU, maybe 9s. The fade callback after 340ms then buildLevel runs and blocks. That's why state level after 10s. Real hardware much faster. So okay.

Full-flow2's 12s timeout was too tight, not a bug. It then broke out and model still "cleared split, model" because it didn't actually clear bunker etc. The script's flow logic was flawed due to timeout. Our timing test with explicit state checks cleared all 4 and no errors. Need still verify model unlock/ending with current code. We can write a final full flow with longer timeouts (30s) and click via evaluate to avoid hidden issues. Or rerun full-flow2 with increased waitState ms. Change `waitState(want, ms=12000)` to 30000. And maybe after `click('#results-btn')`, ensure visible. Let's copy full-flow2 and modify timeout. Use sed.
